family.template_used: not the listed family template -- recovered directly from the assembly as a shop-style quantity-selection dialog loop, sibling to games/gs1/src/shop/select_sale_quantity.c and select_purchase_quantity.c

domain: Opens a small numeric-entry window, marks two menu sub-objects' state byte 5 as 13 (busy), installs Func_080a19a0 as the per-frame update callback, then loops: on D-pad left/right adjusts a running quantity and clamps it through Func_080022fc, redraws it via Func_080a4924, and exits on the Start-equivalent button (Func_080770c0(336)), on A (confirm, keeps quantity) or B (cancel, quantity forced to -1). On exit it tears down both windows, reschedules Func_080a19a0 with a delay, resets the second sub-object's state byte to 1, and returns the final quantity.
notes: The listed family template (08092708, run_rising_sequence.c) was not a useful line-by-line guide; the actual shape -- window create, D-pad quantity loop, A/B confirm-cancel -- was recognized directly from the assembly and matches the surrounding shop quantity-selector siblings in spirit (they call the still-unrecovered Func_080b1614, which this owner is plausibly a component or sibling of).

Reached 292/292 bytes, 0 differing_halfwords (candidate-show --align, fresh compile, class=exact). The prior measured-draft (differing_halfwords=2) had the two button-latch identities swapped: the two trailing literal-pool words at the D-pad-adjust load site and the confirm/cancel-guard load site were transposed relative to the reference. Diffing the linked candidate bytes against the reference .o byte-for-byte (not just the disassembly view) showed the D-pad adjust block (bit tests 0x40/0x80) must take the address of Data_03001b04, and the confirm/cancel guard block (bit tests 1/2, before `done`) must take the address of Data_03001c94 -- the reverse of the previous draft's assignment. Swapping only which extern each scope-local `volatile ... *keys` pointer takes the address of (no other source change) reproduces the reference literal-pool order exactly; this was independently confirmed by extracting the linked candidate bytes at ROM address 0x080a4800 and comparing them to roms/gs1-en.gba directly.

The other two source-shape choices already in place before this fix remain load-bearing: (1) each latch must be read through a scope-local `volatile ... *keys = &Data_...;` pointer reused for its own pair of bit tests, not a macro re-expanded at each use, otherwise GCC hoists the address load out of the block it belongs to; (2) the incoming argument must be declared `s32`, not `u16` -- a narrower parameter type makes the compiler insert an extra sign-extension pair at entry that the reference does not have.

Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, established local function signatures already used elsewhere in the source tree (Func_08015010, Func_080022fc, Func_08015270, Func_08015018, Func_080a2144, Func_080041d8, Func_08015408), and the already-adopted sibling Func_080a19a0 (games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/ui/ui_owner_25.c). No GS2 evidence or external source was used.
